answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a mesa as the anchor of the cost.
